```{=html}
<div id="panel" data-repo="IPBES-Data/IPBES_Data_Vision">

<div class="grid">
  <div class="card">

    <a class="btn" data-workflow="gdoc-import.yml" title="Copies the text and the Document information and Editors tables from the Google Doc. Opens a page listing every change; Merge it to accept, Close it to discard. The website does not change. Form: Doc link (empty = usual Doc).">Import from Google Doc</a>
    <p class="status" data-status="gdoc-import.yml"></p>
  </div>
  <div class="card">
    <h3>2. Export</h3>

The new Doc's link is shown under the run's details. Form: Drive folder (empty = usual folder).">Export to Google Doc</a>
    <p class="status" data-status="gdoc-export.yml"></p>
  </div>
  <div class="card">
    <h3>3. Release</h3>
    <p>Pre-release (review) or release (DOI).</p>
    <a class="btn" data-workflow="release.yml" title="Pre-release: a draft for review, no DOI, shown at the Pre-release preview. Release: a citable version; reserves a DOI and prepares a Zenodo draft, but nothing is public until Publish. Form: type, version (e.g. 1.2), what changed (separate items with ;).">Make a release or pre-release</a>
    <p class="status" data-status="release.yml"></p>
  </div>
  <div class="card">

    <p>Make a prepared release public.</p>

<p class="hint">ℹ️ A button opens the task on GitHub (sign in if asked). There, click <b>Run workflow</b> on the right, fill in the form and click the green <b>Run workflow</b> button. Nothing happens until you do. Hover over a button for details.</p>

<div id="waiting"></div>

<p class="links"><a href="../">Website</a> · <a href="../preview/">Pre-release preview</a> · <a href="../older-releases.html">All releases</a> · <a data-href="/releases">GitHub releases</a> · <a data-href="/pulls">Changes waiting for review</a> · <a href="https://zenodo.org/me/uploads">Zenodo</a> · <a href="https://sandbox.zenodo.org/me/uploads">Zenodo sandbox</a></p>

<style>
/* Each card spans 4 rows of the grid (title, text, button, status) and shares them with its neighbours
   via subgrid, so the buttons line up even when the texts differ in length. */
#panel .grid { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(150px, 1fr)); column-gap: 0.75rem;
               row-gap: 0; margin: 0.5rem 0 1rem; }
#panel .card { border: 1px solid #d7dee6; border-radius: 8px; padding: 0.75rem 1rem; margin-bottom: 0.75rem;
               display: grid; grid-row: span 4; grid-template-rows: subgrid; row-gap: 0.5rem; }
#panel .card h3 { margin: 0; font-size: 1.1rem; }
#panel .card p { margin: 0; }
#panel .btn { align-self: start; }
#panel .btn { display: block; text-align: center; background: #1f6f43; color: #fff; padding: 0.5rem 0.75rem;
              border-radius: 6px; text-decoration: none; font-weight: 600; }
#panel .btn:hover { background: #18583a; }
#panel .card p.status { color: #555; font-size: 0.85rem; }
#panel .waiting { background: #fff6d6; border-radius: 6px; padding: 0.5rem 0.75rem; margin: 0 0 0.5rem; }
#panel .links { font-size: 0.9rem; }
#panel .hint { font-size: 0.9rem; background: #eef4fb; border-radius: 6px; padding: 0.5rem 0.75rem; }
</style>

<script>
(() => {
  const repo = document.getElementById("panel").dataset.repo;
  const gh = `https://github.com/${repo}`;
  const api = (path) => fetch(`https://api.github.com/repos/${repo}${path}`).then((r) => (r.ok ? r.json() : null));
  const link = (href, text) => `<a href="${href}" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">${text}</a>`;
  const waiting = document.getElementById("waiting");
  const notice = (html) => waiting.insertAdjacentHTML("beforeend", `<p class="waiting">${html}</p>`);

  document.querySelectorAll("[data-workflow]").forEach((a) => { a.href = `${gh}/actions/workflows/${a.dataset.workflow}`; });
  document.querySelectorAll("[data-href]").forEach((a) => { a.href = gh + a.dataset.href; });
  document.querySelectorAll("#panel a").forEach((a) => { a.target = "_blank"; a.rel = "noopener noreferrer"; });

  // Last run of each task.
  document.querySelectorAll("[data-status]").forEach(async (p) => {
    const runs = await api(`/actions/workflows/${p.dataset.status}/runs?per_page=1`);
    const run = runs && runs.workflow_runs[0];
    if (!run) { p.textContent = runs ? "Not run yet." : ""; return; }
    const state = run.status !== "completed" ? "⏳ running" :
      run.conclusion === "success" ? "✅ succeeded" : `❌ ${run.conclusion}`;
    p.innerHTML = `${state}, ${new Date(run.created_at).toLocaleString()} · ${link(run.html_url, "details")}`;
  });

  // Imports waiting for review, and releases prepared but not yet published (notes still say "DOI reserved").
  api("/pulls?state=open&per_page=50").then((pulls) => {
    const imports = (pulls || []).filter((p) => p.head.ref.startsWith("google-doc-import-"));
    if (imports.length) notice(`Import waiting for review (step 1): ${imports.map((p) => link(p.html_url, p.title)).join(", ")}`);
  });
  api("/releases?per_page=20").then((releases) => {
    const pending = (releases || []).filter((r) => !r.prerelease && /^DOI reserved:/m.test(r.body || ""));
    if (pending.length) notice(`Release ready to publish (step 4): ${pending.map((r) => link(r.html_url, r.tag_name)).join(", ")}`);
  });
})();
</script>
```

You need to be signed in to GitHub with an account that may edit this repository. Each task takes a few minutes; its status appears above (reload the page).

## What the buttons do

1. **Import from Google Doc** copies the text and the bibliographic tables from the Google Doc. Nothing changes on the website yet: you get a page showing every change, where you accept (**Merge**) or discard (**Close**) it. The form takes a Doc link; leave it empty for the usual Doc.
2. **Export to Google Doc** creates a **new** Google Doc in your Drive with the current text and the bibliographic tables; its link is shown under the run's *details*. Existing Docs are never changed. Paste the new Doc's link into the import form later (or ask the technical admin to make it the usual Doc).
3. **Make a release or pre-release** asks for the type, the version number (e.g. `1.2`) and what changed (items separated by `;`).
   - **Pre-release**: a draft for review. No DOI, archived on GitHub, shown at the *Pre-release preview* link.
   - **Release**: a citable version. A DOI is reserved and a Zenodo draft prepared, but nothing is public until step 4.
4. **Publish release**: after a release in step 3, check the Zenodo draft and the PDF, then publish. This makes the DOI permanent and updates the website. Leave the form empty to publish the newest release.

This panel is always at <https://ipbes-data.github.io/IPBES_Data_Vision/admin/> and is updated whenever the repository changes.

## One-time setup (for the technical admin)

### GitHub

*Settings → Actions → General*: under *Workflow permissions* tick **Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests** (needed by the import). GitHub Pages must serve the `gh-pages` branch.

*Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions*:

| Name | Kind | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `ZENODO_TARGET` | variable | `sandbox` (tests) or `production` (real DOIs) |
| `ZENODO_SANDBOX_TOKEN` | secret | sandbox.zenodo.org token with `deposit:write` and `deposit:actions` |
| `ZENODO_TOKEN` | secret | zenodo.org token with `deposit:write` and `deposit:actions` |
| `GOOGLE_OAUTH` | secret | Google sign-in, created by `scripts/gdoc.py login` (see below) |
| `GDOC_ID` | variable | link or ID of the usual Google Doc to import from |
| `GDRIVE_FOLDER_ID` | variable | optional: link or ID of the Drive folder for exports (default: My Drive) |

People who use the panel need *Write* access to the repository.

### Google (works with a free Google account)

Import and export act as **one Google account** (yours, or a dedicated one): they can read every Doc that account can open, and exports are new Docs owned by it, using its normal Drive storage. Set up once, on a computer with Python:

1. In the [Google Cloud console](https://console.cloud.google.com/), signed in with that account, create a project and enable the **Google Drive API**. No billing is needed.
2. *Google Auth Platform → Branding*: give the app a name (e.g. "IPBES Vision sync") and your e-mail. *Audience*: user type **External**, then **Publish app** (status "In production"). In "Testing" status Google ends the sign-in after 7 days.
3. *Clients → Create client*, type **Desktop app**; download the JSON file (e.g. `client.json`).
4. In this repository run, with the [GitHub CLI](https://cli.github.com/) signed in:

   ```bash
   python3 scripts/gdoc.py login client.json | gh secret set GOOGLE_OAUTH
   ```

   A browser opens; sign in with the Google account. Google warns that the app is not verified: choose *Advanced → Go to IPBES Vision sync* (it is your own app) and allow access to Google Drive. Then delete `client.json`.

If an import or export later fails with "sign-in has expired or was revoked" (e.g. after removing the app's access in the Google account, or after 6 months without use), repeat step 4.

### How the Google Doc must be laid out

Everything before the first heading is the front matter; the text of the Vision starts at the first **Heading 1**.

- **Document information** table, two columns, one row per field: `Title`, `Produced by`, `Publisher`, `Contact e-mail`. All are required; only the second column is edited.
- **Editors** table with the columns `Name | Institution | ORCID`, one row per editor; add or delete rows as needed. Institution and ORCID may be empty; an ORCID may be given as number or as orcid.org link.
- Anything else before the first heading (notes, Google's table of contents) is ignored.
- Section titles use **Heading 1** (sub-sections Heading 2, …). Typed numbers such as "I." or "2.1" in headings are removed; the website and PDF number sections themselves.
- Suggestions must be accepted or rejected before importing; comments are not imported.

If a table is missing or a value is invalid, the import stops without changing anything and lists what to fix (shown under the failed run's *details*).

An export writes exactly this layout, so the easiest start is to run **Export to Google Doc** once and edit the new Doc.

### Zenodo

`ZENODO_TARGET` selects the Zenodo used by releases. The concept DOIs ("all versions" DOI) are in the frontmatter of `IPBES_Data_Vision.qmd` (`zenodo.concept_doi`, `zenodo.sandbox_concept_doi`). Sandbox releases never change the official website. If a prepared release is wrong, delete the draft on Zenodo and the release and its tag on GitHub, then make it again.

### Without the panel

```bash
make preview                                                    # live preview while editing
make build                                                      # website + PDF as unreleased draft
python3 scripts/release.py prepare --version 1.2 --prerelease   # pre-release build, no Zenodo
export GOOGLE_OAUTH="$(python3 scripts/gdoc.py login client.json)"   # sign in once per shell
python3 scripts/gdoc.py import <doc link>
```

## Privacy: Google sign-in "IPBES Vision" {#privacy}

The Google sign-in "IPBES Vision" is used only by the automated tasks of this repository (*Import from Google Doc*, *Export to Google Doc*) to move the text of the IPBES Data Management Vision between this repository and Google Docs in the Google Drive of the account that signed in.

- **What is accessed:** the import opens only the Google Doc it is given and reads its content; the export creates a new Google Doc. No other files are opened, changed or deleted.
- **What is stored:** the imported text and bibliographic information are stored in this public repository, because they are the content of the Vision. Nothing else from Google, and no personal data of Google users, is stored, shared or sold.
- **Where the sign-in is kept:** as an encrypted secret of this GitHub repository, used only by these tasks.
- **Withdrawing access:** at any time at <https://myaccount.google.com/permissions> (remove "IPBES Vision"); import and export then stop working until someone signs in again.
- **Contact:** IPBES.Vision@krugs.de
